title: Why an Octopus Has a Brain in Every Arm
description:
An octopus doesn't have one brain running the show -- it has eight more, one packed into each arm, making decisions the central brain never even finds out about.

#shorts #sciencefacts #octopus #didyouknow

scenes.text: An octopus doesn't really have one brain. It has nine -- a central one, and a smaller brain packed into the base of each of its eight arms.
About two-thirds of an octopus's neurons live in its arms, not its head.
That means each arm can taste and touch what it grabs, and decide how to react, without waiting for a signal from the central brain at all.
Scientists have watched a severed octopus arm keep grabbing at objects on its own, for over an hour -- the arm's local brain runs some of that on its own hardware.
The central brain mostly sends out big-picture instructions, like 'go over there,' and leaves each arm to work out the actual grabbing, climbing, or exploring for itself.
It's less like one mind controlling eight limbs, and more like nine minds that happen to share a body.
If your own hands could think for themselves, do you trust them to make good decisions without you?
